intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing and Swimming in the Caldera
experiences.description: Join a small-group catamaran cruise around Santorini's volcanic caldera, stopping at the Red Beach and White Beach for swimming and snorkeling. The evening departure lets you enjoy the world-famous Oia sunset from the water while avoiding the intense midday heat. Light snacks and local wine are typically included. Indoor alternative: visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera in Fira if weather turns.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita from market vendors. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and pick up ingredients for a picnic. Entirely indoors, making it a perfect rain or heat alternative activity.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Day Trip
experiences.description: Take an early morning boat excursion from Porto Vromi to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed beaches enclosed by towering white cliffs. Arrive before the crowds and midday heat for the best experience. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters and explore the famous rusted shipwreck. Indoor alternative: visit the Byzantine Museum of Zakynthos in the afternoon.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in Crete
experiences.description: Join a hands-on morning cooking class at a family-run farm or taverna in the Cretan countryside. Learn to prepare authentic dishes like dakos (Cretan rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and kalitsounia (cheese pastries) using locally sourced ingredients. Enjoy your creations for lunch with local raki. Held indoors or under shaded pergolas, ideal for avoiding midday heat.

experiences.name: Early Morning Snorkeling at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the stunning pink-sand Elafonissi Beach at sunrise or early morning when the lagoon is calm, uncrowded, and the light is magical. Snorkel through the shallow turquoise lagoon teeming with sea life and explore the small islet connected by a sandbar. Rent snorkel gear locally for a minimal cost. Indoor alternative for midday: explore the nearby Chrysoskalitissa Monastery, a cool stone structure with cultural significance.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from street level. Grab a souvlaki wrap from a street vendor to kick off your Greek food experience.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyro or tiropita (cheese pie) from a bakery near the airport or on arrival
meals.dinner: Street souvlaki wrap with tzatziki from a local kiosk in Monastiraki — around €2–3

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 14:50 arrival. Buy an Ath.ena reloadable transit card at the airport Metro station for cheaper rides throughout your Athens stay. Budget tip: Metro from airport costs ~€9 one-way.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket (~€20) also covers several other archaeological sites — great value. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (covered by the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki flea market for cheap souvenirs and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Psiri neighborhood for dinner. Explore the lively tavernas and ouzeries. Try a mezze spread with local wine or ouzo.

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and Greek coffee from a local bakery — ~€3
meals.lunch: Souvlaki plate with pita, tomatoes, and onions from a local grill near Monastiraki — ~€5–7
meals.dinner: Taverna in Psiri — order shared mezze: tzatziki, taramasalata, grilled octopus, and bread — ~€10–12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the Acropolis right at opening (8:00 AM) to avoid peak heat and tour groups. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The combined archaeological ticket is valid for 5 days — keep it!

day_by_day.morning: Use your combined ticket to visit the Temple of Olympian Zeus and Hadrian's Arch, then walk to the Panathenaic Stadium (Kallimarmaro) — the only stadium in the world built entirely of marble. Exterior viewing is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) — a sensory feast of fresh fish, meat, spices, and olives. Great for budget food shopping and local atmosphere. Then visit the National Garden for a free, shaded afternoon walk.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Thissio or Koukaki neighborhood for dinner — both are slightly off the tourist trail and more affordable. Enjoy views of the Acropolis lit up at night from Thissio's café-lined pedestrian street.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local café — ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Fresh produce, olives, and cheese from the Central Market — assemble a picnic for ~€4–5
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Koukaki — moussaka or pastitsio with a glass of house wine — ~€10–12

day_by_day.notes: The Central Market is closed on Sundays. Koukaki is a great budget-friendly neighborhood with authentic local restaurants away from tourist markup.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Piraeus port to the island of Aegina (about 1 hour, ~€8–10 each way). Rent a bicycle or take a local bus to the stunning Temple of Aphaia — one of Greece's best-preserved ancient temples with panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Aegina Town's waterfront. Swim at Aeginitissa or Marathonas beach — both easily reachable by local bus. Aegina is famous for its pistachios — buy a bag from a local vendor for a cheap, delicious snack.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Piraeus by early evening. Take the Metro back to central Athens. Enjoy a quiet dinner near your hostel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri (sesame bread ring) and coffee before boarding the ferry — ~€2
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or calamari at a waterfront taverna in Aegina Town — ~€8–10
meals.dinner: Simple home-style Greek restaurant near your hostel — stuffed tomatoes (gemista) or lentil soup — ~€7–9

day_by_day.notes: Ferries from Piraeus to Aegina run frequently. Buy tickets at the port kiosk. This is a perfect budget day-trip — Aegina is far less touristy and expensive than the Cyclades islands.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens by early KTEL bus from Kifissos Bus Terminal to Nafplio (~2.5 hours, ~€13). Check into a budget guesthouse in the charming old town. Climb the 999 steps to the Palamidi Fortress for sweeping views over the Argolic Gulf.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's beautiful Venetian old town — stroll through Syntagma Square, browse local shops, and walk along the seaside promenade. Visit the small Bourtzi island fortress visible from the harbor (boat trips available for ~€5).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Nafplio's old town. The town has excellent seafood and traditional Greek cuisine at reasonable prices compared to Athens.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at the bus terminal or on arrival in Nafplio — ~€3
meals.lunch: Souvlaki or gyro from a local grill in Nafplio — ~€4–6
meals.dinner: Seafood taverna near the harbor — grilled sea bream or shrimp saganaki with local wine — ~€12–15

day_by_day.notes: Nafplio is one of Greece's most beautiful towns and very budget-friendly compared to island destinations. The Palamidi climb is free if you walk up (taxi available for ~€5 if needed). Great base for exploring the Peloponnese.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or taxi (~30 min) to the ancient site of Epidaurus. Visit the remarkably preserved ancient theater — one of the best acoustics of any theater in the world. Also explore the Sanctuary of Asclepius. Entry ~€12.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and spend the afternoon at Arvanitia Beach — a small, rocky but beautiful beach just a 10-minute walk from the old town. Free entry, clear turquoise water, perfect for a swim in 23°C weather.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along Nafplio's seaside promenade. Try local street food or grab ice cream from a gelateria. Relax at a waterfront café with a cold Mythos beer.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait and coffee at a café in Nafplio's old town — ~€4
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack from a local bakery before heading to Epidaurus — ~€4–5
meals.dinner: Traditional ouzerie in Nafplio — order a selection of mezze with ouzo or tsipouro — ~€10–12

day_by_day.notes: Epidaurus hosts a famous summer festival of ancient Greek drama — check if any performances coincide with your visit (tickets from ~€15). Arvanitia Beach is free and less crowded than other nearby beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Take a KTEL bus from Nafplio to Corinth (~1.5 hours, ~€7). Visit Ancient Corinth and the impressive Temple of Apollo. The Archaeological Museum on-site is included in the entry fee (~€8).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to the Acrocorinth — the massive medieval fortress perched on a rocky hill above the city. Entry is free and the views are spectacular. Then head to the Corinth Canal viewpoint — one of the most dramatic engineering feats in Greece.
day_by_day.evening: Take a bus or train to Patras or continue toward your next destination. Alternatively, return to Athens for the night if continuing your island journey. Grab dinner at a local taverna in Corinth before departing.

meals.breakfast: Tiropita and coffee from a bakery in Nafplio before departure — ~€3
meals.lunch: Simple taverna near Ancient Corinth — Greek salad, bread, and grilled meat — ~€8–10
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Corinth or on arrival at next stop — pasta or grilled chicken — ~€8–10

day_by_day.notes: Corinth is an easy and rewarding day trip. The Acrocorinth is free to enter and often overlooked by tourists — you may have it nearly to yourself. Budget tip: trains between Corinth and Athens run regularly for ~€5.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to the port of Piraeus (Athens) and take a budget ferry to the island of Paros (~4–5 hours on a standard ferry, ~€25–35). Book in advance for best prices. Arrive in Parikia, the island's main town, and check into a budget room or hostel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Parikia's charming whitewashed old town. Visit the Panagia Ekatontapiliani — one of the oldest and most important Byzantine churches in Greece (free entry). Stroll through the narrow marble-paved alleys.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the Venetian Kastro ruins overlooking the sea. Have dinner at a local taverna in Parikia — Paros is more affordable than Mykonos or Santorini.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack on the ferry or at Piraeus port before boarding — ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Cheese pie or spanakopita from a bakery in Parikia on arrival — ~€3
meals.dinner: Fresh fish taverna in Parikia — grilled octopus, Greek salad, and local wine — ~€12–15

day_by_day.notes: Paros is one of the best value Cycladic islands — beautiful beaches, great food, and far less expensive than Mykonos or Santorini. Book ferry tickets at least a few days in advance during June. Standard (slow) ferries are much cheaper than high-speed ones.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or bicycle (~€10–15/day) and explore the island. Head to the beautiful village of Naoussa in the north — a picturesque fishing village with a Venetian harbor, whitewashed houses, and excellent local restaurants.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Naoussa, visit Kolymbithres Beach — famous for its unique granite rock formations and crystal-clear water. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing. The beach is accessible by local bus or a short scooter ride.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Parikia for the evening. Explore the waterfront and enjoy a leisurely dinner. Try fresh grilled fish or the local specialty — Parian goat cheese.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and koulouri at a café in Parikia — ~€2–3
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood mezze at a small taverna in Naoussa harbor — ~€10–12
meals.dinner: Budget taverna in Parikia — lamb chops or stuffed peppers with local Parian wine — ~€10–13

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental is the best way to explore Paros on a budget. Always wear a helmet. Kolymbithres is one of the most unique beaches in the Cyclades — arrive before noon for the best spots. June weather (~23°C) is ideal for beach days.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short ferry or water taxi from Paros to the small island of Antiparos (~15 min, ~€2). Explore the charming main village and the impressive Cave of Antiparos — one of the largest sea caves in Europe, with stalactites thousands of years old. Entry ~€4.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on one of Antiparos's beautiful, uncrowded beaches — Sifneikos or Glyfa are excellent choices. The water is calm and clear, perfect for snorkeling. Antiparos is quieter and more laid-back than Paros.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Paros by ferry. Enjoy your last evening on the island with a sunset dinner. Pack your bags for the next day's travel.

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread, local honey, and coffee at a café in Parikia — ~€4
meals.lunch: Simple taverna in Antiparos village — Greek salad, grilled sardines, and bread — ~€8–10
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Parikia — try fresh grilled sea bass with lemon and olive oil — ~€12–14

day_by_day.notes: Antiparos is a hidden gem — far less crowded than most Cycladic islands. The cave is worth the visit. Bring cash as some small establishments on Antiparos don't accept cards. Water taxis run frequently from Parikia port.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early ferry from Paros to Naxos (~45 min, ~€10) — the largest and most fertile of the Cyclades. Check into budget accommodation in Naxos Town (Chora). Visit the iconic Portara — the massive marble doorway of an unfinished ancient temple on a small islet connected to the harbor by a causeway. Free to visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Naxos Town's medieval Kastro — a Venetian fortified hilltop neighborhood with narrow alleys, a Catholic cathedral, and a small archaeological museum (~€3). Browse the local shops for Naxian products: thyme honey, kitron liqueur, and local cheeses.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the waterfront for dinner. Naxos is famous for its local produce — try dishes featuring Naxian potatoes, graviera cheese, and fresh seafood.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee on the ferry or upon arrival in Naxos — ~€3
meals.lunch: Gyro or souvlaki from a local grill in Naxos Town — ~€4–5
meals.dinner: Waterfront taverna in Naxos — try loukoumades (honey doughnuts) for dessert — ~€11–14

day_by_day.notes: Naxos is arguably the best value Cycladic island — it produces its own food so prices are lower than other islands. The Portara at sunset is one of the most magical sights in Greece. Free to visit at any time.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or take a local bus to explore Naxos's stunning west coast beaches. Start at Agios Prokopios — a long, sandy, Blue Flag beach with calm, shallow water. Then continue to Agia Anna and Plaka Beach — one of the longest and most beautiful beaches in the Cyclades.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south to Mikri Vigla or Kastraki Beach for a more secluded experience. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying the 23°C weather. The beaches on Naxos are among the best in Greece and largely free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Naxos Town for your final island evening. Explore the old market street (Papavasiliou) for local products to take home. Enjoy a celebratory farewell dinner with local wine.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with Naxian thyme honey at a café in Naxos Town — ~€4
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Plaka — fresh calamari, Greek salad, and cold beer — ~€10–12
meals.dinner: Traditional Naxian restaurant — try the local specialty 'marides' (fried whitebait) and Naxian graviera cheese — ~€12–15

day_by_day.notes: Naxos beaches are consistently ranked among Greece's best. Plaka Beach is 8km long — you'll easily find a quiet spot. Local buses run regularly from Naxos Town to the beach strip. Buy a small bottle of kitron liqueur as a souvenir — it's unique to Naxos.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning ferry back to Piraeus (Athens) — approximately 5–6 hours on a standard ferry (~€30–40). Enjoy the scenic Aegean views from the deck. Arrive in Athens by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time allows before your departure, revisit a favorite Athens neighborhood or do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the Monastiraki flea market. Pick up local products: olive oil, herbs, honey, or worry beads (komboloi) as gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Athens International Airport for your return flight. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure. Reflect on 13 incredible days of Greek beaches, ancient history, and delicious local food.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and tiropita from a bakery in Naxos before boarding the ferry — ~€3
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry or grab a quick bite near Piraeus on arrival — ~€5–6
meals.dinner: Final meal at a budget taverna near the airport or a quick souvlaki at the airport — ~€8–10

day_by_day.notes: Book your return ferry from Naxos to Piraeus in advance. Standard ferries are significantly cheaper than high-speed options. Keep some cash for the airport. Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights): €600–800 per person, covering accommodation in budget hostels/guesthouses, local transport, ferry tickets, entry fees, and meals.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita from market vendors. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and pick up ingredients for a picnic. Entirely indoors, making it a perfect rain or heat alternative activity.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 to central Athens. Check in to your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Syntagma area. Freshen up and take a gentle orientation stroll around Monastiraki Square and the Roman Agora to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric Plaka neighborhood — the oldest district in Athens. Explore the narrow, lamp-lit streets, browse local shops for olive oil and ceramics, and soak in the ambiance beneath the Acropolis.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the airport or a souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk near Monastiraki (€3–5)
meals.dinner: Taverna To Kafeneio in Plaka — try moussaka, grilled octopus, and a carafe of house wine. Budget approx €18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real — prioritize settling in. Keep the evening walk short and relaxed. Book your hotel near Monastiraki for easy access to all central Athens sights.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour — join the available 'Athens Central Market Food Tour' experience at the historic Varvakios Agora. A local guide leads you through stalls of fresh fish, spices, olives, cheeses, and cured meats. Sample local delicacies and learn about Greek culinary traditions. Tours typically run 9:00–12:00. Cost approx €45–55 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon (book tickets online in advance, €20). Arrive by 13:00 to beat the peak afternoon heat. Explore the Propylaea, Erechtheion, and Temple of Athena Nike. Afterward, visit the world-class Acropolis Museum at the base of the hill (€10).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Thisio neighborhood for sunset views of the Acropolis from the pedestrian promenade on Apostolou Pavlou street. Enjoy a relaxed evening in this trendy, quieter district.

meals.breakfast: Included tastings during the food tour, or grab a bougatsa (custard pastry) and Greek coffee at a local bakery before the tour (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch at a taverna near the Acropolis Museum — try tzatziki, spanakopita, and dolmades (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Stavlos in Thisio — a converted royal stable turned restaurant/bar with a lovely courtyard. Try lamb chops and Greek salad (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The food tour is the highlight of the day — arrive hungry! Book Acropolis tickets online to skip the queue. Wear comfortable shoes with good grip for the marble surfaces on the Acropolis.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ancient Agora of Athens (€10) — the heart of ancient Athenian civic life. Explore the remarkably preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Quieter and less crowded than the Acropolis, this is a gem. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the tram or bus to Glyfada beach (approx 30 min from central Athens) — a popular, well-organized beach on the Athens Riviera with clear water, sunbeds, and beach bars. Enjoy a long, relaxing afternoon swim. Average June temperature: 23°C — perfect beach weather.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens and explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood. Browse boutiques and enjoy the lively café culture. This is a great area for people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts at a neighborhood café near your hotel (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beach taverna in Glyfada — grilled sea bream with lemon and olive oil, Greek salad (€18–24)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) in Kolonaki — order a spread of small plates: fava, taramosalata, grilled halloumi, and shrimp saganaki (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Glyfada has both free public beach sections and paid beach clubs (sunbed rental €8–15). The tram from Syntagma to Glyfada is scenic and affordable (€1.40). Check the weather — June can occasionally have brief afternoon showers.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Cape Sounion — take a KTEL bus from Pedion Areos park (€6.50 each way, 1.5 hrs). Visit the stunning Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff 60m above the Aegean Sea. Lord Byron carved his name in the marble here. Arrive early (9:00) before tour groups. Entry €10.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, stop at Vouliagmeni Lake — a unique brackish thermal lake fed by underground springs, set in a rocky cove. Swim in the mineral-rich waters (entry €15). The water is a constant 22–29°C and said to have therapeutic properties.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by early evening. Relax and enjoy a quiet dinner in the Psyrri neighborhood — Athens' bohemian arts district with excellent street food and casual restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Grab a tiropita (cheese pie) and coffee from a bakery before catching the bus (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack at the Cape Sounion café/taverna with views of the temple (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Psyrri taverna — try slow-cooked lamb kleftiko, village bread, and local Assyrtiko white wine (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Cape Sounion bus departs roughly every hour from Pedion Areos. Combine the visit with Vouliagmeni on the return for a full and rewarding day. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water — the cape is exposed and sunny.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the ferry from Piraeus port to Santorini (Thira). High-speed ferry takes approx 5 hours (book in advance, €55–75). Depart around 7:30 AM — take the Metro from central Athens to Piraeus (Line 1, €1.40). Enjoy the open sea crossing with views of the Cyclades islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Santorini at Athinios port around 12:30–13:00. Take the local bus or shared taxi to Fira (the island's capital). Check in to your mid-range hotel — look for options in Fira or Firostefani for caldera views without the Oia price premium. Explore Fira's winding clifftop streets.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the caldera path from Fira toward Firostefani and Imerovigli for spectacular sunset views over the volcanic caldera. This is one of the most dramatic landscapes in the Mediterranean.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Athens hotel or grab pastries at Piraeus port (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Light meal on the ferry or a quick gyros wrap upon arriving in Fira (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Metaxy Mas in Exo Gonia (short taxi ride) — a beloved local taverna known for authentic Santorinian cuisine: fava, white eggplant, and fresh fish (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets well in advance for June — Santorini is extremely popular. Arrive at Piraeus port at least 45 minutes before departure. The high-speed catamaran is faster but pricier than the standard ferry. Confirm your hotel has a shuttle from the port or arrange a taxi.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Oia village — take the local bus (€1.80) or a 10km scenic walk along the caldera rim from Fira. Oia is famous for its iconic blue-domed churches, cave houses, and art galleries. Visit early (before 10:00) to enjoy it before the cruise ship crowds arrive. Browse the artisan shops and photography galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Amoudi Bay — descend the 300 steps below Oia to this tiny fishing harbor. Swim in the crystal-clear volcanic waters directly from the rocks. Several excellent seafood tavernas line the bay.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Oia for the world-famous Santorini sunset — arrive by 19:00 to secure a good viewing spot near the castle ruins (Kasteli). The sunset here is genuinely spectacular. Return to Fira by bus or taxi.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a café in Fira with caldera views — Greek coffee, eggs, and fresh fruit (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled octopus and local white wine at one of the Amoudi Bay tavernas — Sunset Taverna or Dimitris (€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner back in Fira — try a local gyros or souvlaki place to balance the budget after the splurge lunch (€8–12)

day_by_day.notes: The Fira-to-Oia caldera walk is stunning but takes 3–4 hours and is exposed to sun — start very early or take the bus and walk back. Oia gets extremely crowded at sunset; arrive early or watch from a quieter spot along the caldera path.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Akrotiri Archaeological Site — a remarkably preserved Bronze Age city buried by the volcanic eruption of 1627 BC, often called the 'Minoan Pompeii.' Entry €12. Hire an audio guide for context. The site is covered and cool — ideal for a morning visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Red Beach (Kokkini Paralia) near Akrotiri — one of Greece's most dramatic beaches, with towering red and black volcanic cliffs. The water is clear and deep. Note: access involves a short rocky walk. Alternatively, visit Perissa Black Sand Beach on the south coast for a longer, more comfortable beach day with sunbeds and beach bars.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the village of Pyrgos — Santorini's highest village, with a medieval Venetian castle, traditional architecture, and fewer tourists. Enjoy a quiet evening with panoramic island views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar near Red Beach or Perissa — fresh sandwiches, salads, and cold drinks (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Franco's Café or a local taverna in Pyrgos — try slow-roasted pork with local capers and tomato fritters (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Red Beach can be accessed by water taxi from Akrotiri port (€5 return) or by a short rocky footpath. Perissa is better for families and those wanting full beach facilities. Rent a quad bike or ATV (€25–35/day) to explore the south of the island independently.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Ferry from Santorini to Mykonos (approx 2–2.5 hours by high-speed ferry, €40–60). Depart around 9:00 AM. Arrive in Mykonos Town (Chora) by late morning. Check in to your mid-range hotel — look for options in or near Mykonos Town for easy access to beaches and nightlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Mykonos Town (Chora) — wander the iconic labyrinthine whitewashed alleys designed to confuse pirates. Visit the famous windmills (Kato Mili) overlooking the sea, and the charming Little Venice neighborhood where the houses hang over the water. Browse the boutiques and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the legendary Mykonos sunset from Little Venice — the bars and cafés here fill up for the golden hour. The view of the windmills and the Aegean is iconic.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast on the ferry or at a café in Mykonos Town upon arrival (€6–10)
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch at a harbor-side taverna in Mykonos Town — try grilled red mullet with lemon and capers (€18–24)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nikos Taverna in Mykonos Town — a beloved local institution serving traditional Greek dishes at reasonable prices for Mykonos: stuffed peppers, lamb chops, fresh salads (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mykonos is the most expensive of the three islands on this itinerary — budget accordingly. Book accommodation well in advance. The town's streets are intentionally confusing — embrace getting lost, it's part of the charm. Download an offline map.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Delos — take the short boat from Mykonos Town harbor (€20 return, 30 min). Delos is one of the most important archaeological sites in Greece — the mythological birthplace of Apollo and Artemis. Explore the ancient ruins, the Terrace of the Lions, and the mosaic-floored houses. Allow 3–4 hours. Bring water and a hat — there is no shade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos and head to Paradise Beach or Paraga Beach — two of Mykonos' most famous beaches on the south coast. Take the local bus (€2) or water taxi. Paraga is slightly quieter than Paradise. Rent a sunbed (€10–15) and enjoy the turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for the evening. Explore the Matogianni Street shopping area and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere as the island comes alive after dark.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt and honey at a café before catching the Delos boat (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Delos (limited options — bring snacks) or a quick meal back in Mykonos Town before heading to the beach (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Joanna's Nikos Place in Megali Ammos — a family-run taverna with excellent fresh fish and traditional dishes at fair prices for Mykonos (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Delos is closed on Mondays — check the schedule before planning. Entry to Delos is €12. The site is entirely exposed to the sun — start early and bring at least 1.5L of water per person. The last boat back to Mykonos is typically around 15:00.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or ATV (€25–40/day) and explore Mykonos independently. Head to the quieter northern beaches: Panormos Beach and Agios Sostis Beach — both are undeveloped, with no sunbeds or bars, offering a more natural and peaceful experience. The drive through the island's interior is scenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Fokos Beach on the northeast coast — one of Mykonos' most secluded and beautiful beaches, accessible only by dirt road. Crystal-clear water, minimal crowds, and a single traditional taverna. Spend a long, lazy afternoon here.
day_by_day.evening: Return the scooter and spend your last Mykonos evening in Little Venice. Enjoy cocktails at a waterfront bar as the sun sets, then have a final dinner in Chora.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a bakery in Mykonos Town — fresh bread, cheese, and coffee (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch at the simple taverna at Fokos Beach — whatever the fishermen brought in that morning, grilled simply with olive oil and lemon (€18–24)
meals.dinner: Dinner at M-eating in Mykonos Town — creative Greek cuisine with local ingredients, excellent wine list (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental requires a valid driving license. Roads in Mykonos can be narrow and busy in summer — drive carefully. Agios Sostis and Fokos have no facilities — bring water, snacks, and sunscreen. These beaches are worth the effort for their natural beauty.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Ferry from Mykonos back to Athens (Piraeus) — high-speed ferry approx 2.5–3.5 hours (€45–65). Depart around 8:00–9:00 AM. Arrive in Piraeus by midday. Take the Metro back to central Athens. Check back in to your Athens hotel (or a different one for variety — consider the Exarchia or Koukaki neighborhoods).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Archaeological Museum — one of the greatest museums in the world, housing treasures from across ancient Greece including the Antikythera Mechanism, the Mask of Agamemnon, and stunning bronze sculptures. Entry €15. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Exarchia neighborhood — Athens' alternative, intellectual district with street art, independent bookshops, and excellent casual restaurants. Very different in character from the tourist areas.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Mykonos hotel or grab pastries at the port (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the National Archaeological Museum — a neighborhood psistaria (grill house) serving souvlaki plates and salads (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Exarchia at Rozalia — a classic, no-frills taverna with a garden courtyard, serving excellent traditional Greek food at very fair prices (€14–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Tuesdays — check the schedule. If arriving back in Athens tired from island-hopping, feel free to skip the museum and simply rest and explore the neighborhood at a leisurely pace.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Benaki Museum — a superb private museum covering Greek history from prehistoric times to the 20th century, housed in a beautiful neoclassical mansion. Entry €9. The rooftop café has excellent views. Allow 2 hours. Afterward, stroll through the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the funicular (teleferik) up Lycabettus Hill — the highest point in Athens at 277m. The views over the entire city, the Acropolis, and the Saronic Gulf are extraordinary. Walk back down through the pine-forested paths. Then visit the Panathenaic Stadium (Kallimarmaro) — the original Olympic stadium built entirely of white marble, used in the 1896 Olympics. Entry €10.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens — return to the Monastiraki area for a farewell stroll through the flea market (open late on weekends) and a final dinner in the neighborhood you've come to love.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a Kolonaki café — eggs, fresh orange juice, and Greek coffee (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Benaki Museum rooftop café — light Mediterranean dishes with city views (€14–18)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Diporto Agoras — a legendary, hidden basement taverna near the Central Market with no menu, just whatever is fresh that day. Cash only, extremely local, unforgettable (€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Diporto Agoras is one of Athens' most authentic dining experiences — it has no sign, no menu, and no credit cards. Ask a local or your hotel to help you find it. It's typically open for lunch and early dinner only. Adjust your dinner timing accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — pack and check out of your hotel. If your flight is in the afternoon, store luggage at the hotel or at a luggage storage service near Syntagma. Take a final walk to the Acropolis viewpoint at Filopappou Hill for a last look at the Parthenon. Visit a local bakery for one last Greek coffee and koulouri (sesame bread ring).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) one last time to pick up food souvenirs: vacuum-packed olives, Greek honey, dried herbs, and local cheeses. Head to the airport via Metro Line 3 from Syntagma (45 min, €10.50 for airport ticket). Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Athens International Airport. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — a proper sit-down meal at a neighborhood café: Greek coffee, fresh orange juice, tiropita, and yogurt with honey (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Central Market or at the airport — a final souvlaki wrap or spanakopita (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner on the plane or at the airport if time allows

day_by_day.notes: Athens Airport Metro tickets cost €10.50 (different from the standard €1.40 city ticket). The journey takes approximately 40–45 minutes from Syntagma. Allow extra time for check-in and security. Great food souvenirs to bring home: Kalamata olives, Cretan thyme honey, mastiha products, dried oregano, and local wine.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing and Swimming in the Caldera
experiences.description: Join a small-group catamaran cruise around Santorini's volcanic caldera, stopping at the Red Beach and White Beach for swimming and snorkeling. The evening departure lets you enjoy the world-famous Oia sunset from the water while avoiding the intense midday heat. Light snacks and local wine are typically included. Indoor alternative: visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera in Fira if weather turns.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita from market vendors. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and pick up ingredients for a picnic. Entirely indoors, making it a perfect rain or heat alternative activity.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Day Trip
experiences.description: Take an early morning boat excursion from Porto Vromi to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed beaches enclosed by towering white cliffs. Arrive before the crowds and midday heat for the best experience. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters and explore the famous rusted shipwreck. Indoor alternative: visit the Byzantine Museum of Zakynthos in the afternoon.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in Crete
experiences.description: Join a hands-on morning cooking class at a family-run farm or taverna in the Cretan countryside. Learn to prepare authentic dishes like dakos (Cretan rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and kalitsounia (cheese pastries) using locally sourced ingredients. Enjoy your creations for lunch with local raki. Held indoors or under shaded pergolas, ideal for avoiding midday heat.

experiences.name: Early Morning Snorkeling at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the stunning pink-sand Elafonissi Beach at sunrise or early morning when the lagoon is calm, uncrowded, and the light is magical. Snorkel through the shallow turquoise lagoon teeming with sea life and explore the small islet connected by a sandbar. Rent snorkel gear locally for a minimal cost. Indoor alternative for midday: explore the nearby Chrysoskalitissa Monastery, a cool stone structure with cultural significance.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 via Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your five-star hotel in the Plaka or Kolonaki district of Athens. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely stroll through the atmospheric Plaka neighborhood beneath the illuminated Acropolis. Enjoy a relaxed first evening soaking in the ambiance of Athens at night.

meals.breakfast: Meal served on flight
meals.lunch: Meal served on flight or light snack at airport arrivals lounge
meals.dinner: Dinner at Varoulko Seaside (Michelin-starred, modern Greek seafood cuisine) in Piraeus or Hytra rooftop restaurant in Athens — reserve in advance. Expect fresh Aegean fish, sea urchin pasta, and curated Greek wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer. Confirm hotel check-in time. Keep Day 1 light given afternoon arrival and potential travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour — Join a private or small-group guided tour of the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in the cool morning hours. Explore stalls overflowing with fresh fish, cured meats, spices, olives, and local cheeses. Sample traditional Greek street foods including koulouri, loukoumades, and fresh-cut fruit. Learn about the history of Greek culinary traditions from your expert local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon with a private licensed archaeologist guide, avoiding the midday crowds. Follow with a visit to the world-class Acropolis Museum, where you can view original friezes and artifacts in an air-conditioned, architecturally stunning setting.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in Monastiraki with direct Acropolis views (Galaxy Bar at Hilton or A for Athens rooftop). Then dinner in the upscale Kolonaki district.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast buffet featuring Greek yogurt with Cretan honey, fresh pastries, cold cuts, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Light meze lunch at a traditional taverna near the Central Market — try grilled octopus, taramosalata, and spanakopita paired with chilled Assyrtiko white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spondi (two Michelin stars) — refined French-Mediterranean cuisine with an exceptional Greek wine cellar. Tasting menu recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and Spondi restaurant well in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the market tour and Acropolis visit. Best to arrive at the Acropolis before 10:00 AM to beat heat and crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Ancient Agora of Athens and the Temple of Hephaestus — one of the best-preserved ancient Greek temples. Explore the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the charming Thissio neighborhood with its neoclassical architecture and café-lined pedestrian promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Archaeological Museum, home to the world's finest collection of ancient Greek antiquities including the Antikythera Mechanism and Mycenaean gold masks. Spend 2–3 hours with a private guide for context and depth.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood for boutique shopping (Greek designers, jewelry, olive oil products). Enjoy a pre-dinner aperitif at a stylish wine bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a visit to a traditional Greek kafeneion for fresh tiropita (cheese pie), Greek coffee, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Lunch at Diporto Agoras — a legendary, no-frills underground taverna near the Central Market beloved by locals. Try the chickpea soup and grilled fish of the day.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nolan Athens — innovative Japanese-Greek fusion cuisine in a chic setting. Try the wagyu with miso and Greek herbs, paired with natural Greek wines.

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Tuesdays — verify schedule. Consider purchasing a combined archaeological sites ticket for savings across Athens monuments.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Athens port (Piraeus) and board a high-speed ferry or private yacht charter to Santorini (approximately 5–8 hours by ferry or 30 minutes by domestic flight — consider flying for comfort). Alternatively, take an early morning Olympic Air or Sky Express flight from Athens to Santorini (Thira Airport) for a 45-minute scenic flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Santorini and transfer to your luxury cave hotel in Oia or Imerovigli (e.g., Canaves Oia Epitome, Andronis Luxury Suites, or Mystique). Check in and enjoy your private infinity pool overlooking the caldera. Rest and acclimatize to the island's magic.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the iconic village of Oia on foot — browse art galleries, jewelry boutiques, and local ceramics shops. Find your perfect spot to watch the world-famous Santorini sunset over the caldera.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab fresh koulouri and coffee at a bakery near Piraeus port before departure
meals.lunch: Light lunch on board the ferry or at the airport lounge, or upon arrival at a caldera-view café in Fira
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lauda Restaurant at Andronis Luxury Suites in Oia — exceptional caldera views, refined Greek cuisine, and an award-winning wine list featuring Santorini's volcanic Assyrtiko wines

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry or flight tickets well in advance for June travel. Pre-arrange private transfer from Santorini port or airport to hotel — the roads are narrow and steep. Confirm hotel has porter service for luggage.

day_by_day.morning: Sunset Sailing and Swimming in the Caldera — Join a private or small-group luxury catamaran cruise around Santorini's volcanic caldera. Depart in the morning to beat crowds. Stop at the iconic Red Beach (dramatic red volcanic cliffs), White Beach, and the hot springs near the volcanic island of Nea Kameni. Swim, snorkel, and soak in the geothermal waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the catamaran cruise with a stop at the submerged volcanic crater for swimming. Enjoy a gourmet lunch served on deck with fresh Greek salad, grilled meats, local cheeses, and chilled Santorini wine. Sail back along the caldera cliffs as the afternoon light turns golden.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel for a relaxing sunset from your private terrace or infinity pool. Enjoy a spa treatment at the hotel's wellness center (volcanic stone massage or Aegean sea salt scrub).

meals.breakfast: Luxurious hotel breakfast on your private terrace — fresh pastries, local honey, Santorini cherry tomatoes, fava dip, and eggs prepared to order
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch served on the catamaran deck — fresh Greek mezedes, grilled seafood, and Santorini Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Selene Restaurant in Pyrgos village — one of Santorini's most celebrated restaurants, focusing on elevated traditional Cycladic cuisine using local ingredients like fava, capers, and white eggplant

day_by_day.notes: Book the private catamaran charter in advance — private charters offer a far superior experience to crowded group tours. Apply high-SPF sunscreen and bring a hat. The hot springs can stain swimwear.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a private driver or ATV to explore Santorini's lesser-visited villages. Visit Pyrgos (the island's highest point) for panoramic views, then explore the medieval village of Emporio with its Venetian castle ruins. Stop at a local winery (Santo Wines or Domaine Sigalas) for a private barrel-tasting of Assyrtiko, Nykteri, and Vinsanto dessert wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by the volcanic eruption of 1627 BC, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' Explore with a private guide. Afterward, relax at Perivolos or Perissa black-sand beach with a sunbed and cocktail service.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Oia for a final evening. Browse the boutique shops and art galleries. Watch the sunset from the Oia Castle ruins (arrive early to secure a good spot).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional taverna in Pyrgos village — try slow-cooked lamb, local fava bean puree, and Santorini's famous cherry tomato salad
meals.dinner: Dinner at 1800 Restaurant in Oia — housed in a beautifully restored 19th-century captain's mansion, serving refined Greek cuisine with an exceptional wine list and caldera views

day_by_day.notes: Akrotiri requires advance ticket booking in peak season. The site is partially covered, making it comfortable even in warm weather. Winery visits should be booked in advance for private tastings.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast on your hotel terrace, take a final dip in your infinity pool, and pack for departure. Check out of your Santorini hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short domestic flight or high-speed ferry from Santorini to Zakynthos (via Athens connection if needed) or take a scenic ferry to Crete (Heraklion). For this itinerary, fly to Heraklion, Crete (approximately 45 minutes). Transfer to your luxury hotel — consider Domes of Elounda, Blue Palace Elounda, or Amirandes Grecotel near Heraklion or Elounda.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your Cretan luxury resort. Take an evening walk along the Venetian harbor of Heraklion or relax at the hotel's beach club. Enjoy the slower, more authentic pace of Crete.

meals.breakfast: Final lavish hotel breakfast in Santorini
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Heraklion airport or upon arrival at a harbor-front café in Heraklion — try dakos (Cretan rusk salad) and fresh grilled fish
meals.dinner: Dinner at Peskesi Restaurant in Heraklion — a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant dedicated to authentic Cretan cuisine using heirloom ingredients. Try the slow-cooked lamb with stamnagathi greens and aged Cretan graviera cheese.

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flights well in advance. Confirm hotel transfer from Heraklion airport. Crete is a large island — choose your base wisely based on planned activities (Elounda for luxury resort experience, Chania for culture and beaches).

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in Crete — Join a hands-on morning cooking class at a family-run farm or taverna in the Cretan countryside. Learn to prepare traditional Cretan dishes including dakos, kalitsounia (herb-filled pastries), slow-cooked lamb with artichokes, and loukoumades with thyme honey. Visit the farm's olive grove, herb garden, and vegetable patch. Learn about the Cretan diet — one of the world's healthiest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palace of Knossos — the legendary Minoan palace complex dating back to 1700 BC, associated with the myth of the Minotaur and the Labyrinth. Explore with a private archaeologist guide. Follow with a visit to the Heraklion Archaeological Museum, home to the world's finest Minoan art collection.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your resort for a sunset cocktail at the beach bar. Enjoy the warm Cretan evening air.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast before the cooking class
meals.lunch: Feast on the dishes you prepared during the cooking class — a multi-course Cretan lunch paired with local wine and raki
meals.dinner: Dinner at your resort's signature restaurant or at Avli Restaurant in Rethymno (if day-tripping) — elegant Cretan cuisine in a romantic garden courtyard setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance — private farm experiences book up quickly in June. Wear comfortable clothes for the cooking class. Knossos is best visited with a guide to fully appreciate the complex mythology and history.

day_by_day.morning: Early Morning Snorkeling at Elafonissi Beach — Depart early (6:30–7:00 AM) by private car for the 1.5-hour drive to the stunning Elafonissi Beach on Crete's southwestern tip. Arrive at sunrise when the lagoon is calm, the pink-tinged sand glows in the morning light, and the beach is virtually empty. Snorkel in the crystal-clear shallow lagoon, exploring the colorful marine life and unique pink sand formed from crushed shells and coral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the late morning and early afternoon relaxing on Elafonissi's pristine beach before the crowds arrive. Wade through the shallow lagoon to the small island. Explore the surrounding coastal landscape. Begin the return drive to your hotel in the early afternoon, stopping at a traditional Cretan village along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening at your luxury resort — spa treatment, sunset swim, and a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — Greek yogurt, honey, and fresh fruit to go
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by your hotel or a simple meal at a local taverna near Elafonissi — fresh grilled fish, village salad, and local bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at your resort's fine dining restaurant — enjoy fresh Cretan seafood, local cheeses, and a bottle of Cretan Vidiano white wine

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is a 2-hour drive from Heraklion — consider staying in Chania for easier access. Bring snorkeling gear (or rent on-site), reef-safe sunscreen, and plenty of water. Arrive before 8:00 AM for the best experience before crowds arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the enchanting old town of Chania — one of Greece's most beautiful cities. Wander through the Venetian harbor with its iconic lighthouse, explore the covered market (Agora), browse the narrow lanes of the old Jewish quarter (Evraiki), and visit the Maritime Museum of Crete. Hire a private guide for historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat excursion from Chania to the secluded Balos Lagoon and Gramvousa Island — a stunning turquoise lagoon with white sand and a Venetian fortress. Swim in the impossibly blue waters and explore the ruins of the fortress. Return by boat in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a harbor-front bar in Chania's Venetian harbor. Browse the artisan shops for Cretan leather goods, olive wood products, and local honey.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a harbor-front taverna in Chania — grilled sea bream, shrimp saganaki, and Cretan wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tamam Restaurant in Chania — housed in a converted Ottoman bathhouse, serving creative Mediterranean cuisine with strong Cretan influences in a uniquely atmospheric setting

day_by_day.notes: Balos Lagoon boat trips depart from Kissamos port — book in advance. Alternatively, Balos can be reached by a rough road and short hike, but the boat excursion is more comfortable and scenic. Chania old town is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Heraklion (or Chania) to Zakynthos (Zante) via Athens — approximately 2–3 hours total travel time including connection. Alternatively, take a scenic ferry. Transfer to your luxury villa or boutique hotel on Zakynthos (consider Villa Ionian Blue or a private villa rental in the Vassilikos peninsula).
day_by_day.afternoon: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Day Trip — Take an afternoon boat excursion from Porto Vromi to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed locations. The beach is accessible only by boat and features the rusting wreck of the MV Panagiotis surrounded by towering white limestone cliffs and impossibly turquoise water. Swim, snorkel, and photograph this extraordinary natural wonder.
day_by_day.evening: Return from Navagio Beach and settle into your Zakynthos accommodation. Enjoy a relaxed evening watching the sunset over the Ionian Sea.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Crete before departure
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Zakynthos airport or upon arrival at a local café
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malanos Restaurant in Zakynthos Town — a beloved local institution serving traditional Zakynthian cuisine including sofrito (veal in white wine and garlic sauce) and pastitsada, paired with local Verdea white wine

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach boat trips from Porto Vromi take approximately 15–20 minutes each way. Book a private boat for the best experience. The beach can get crowded in the afternoon — if possible, arrange an early morning visit on Day 12 instead. Verify flight connections carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning boat trip to the Blue Caves (Kyanoun Spileon) on the northern tip of Zakynthos — extraordinary sea caves where the water glows an ethereal electric blue due to light refraction. Swim inside the caves and snorkel in the crystal-clear Ionian waters. The morning light (8:00–10:00 AM) creates the most spectacular blue effect.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at one of Zakynthos's premium beaches — Gerakas Beach (a protected loggerhead sea turtle nesting site) or Porto Zoro Beach on the Vassilikos peninsula. Enjoy sunbeds, crystal-clear water, and the relaxed Ionian atmosphere. Optional: visit the Zakynthos Marine Park information center to learn about the endangered loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta) that nest on the island's beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) — visit the Byzantine Museum, stroll along the elegant Venetian-influenced waterfront, and browse local shops for nougat (mandolato), olive oil, and local wines.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the Blue Caves boat trip — Greek yogurt and coffee at your villa or hotel
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside taverna on the Vassilikos peninsula — grilled lobster, fresh calamari, and village salad
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Zakanthi Restaurant — elegant setting with panoramic views, serving refined Greek cuisine with an emphasis on fresh local seafood and Ionian specialties

day_by_day.notes: Blue Caves boat trips depart from Agios Nikolaos village in the north — arrange private boat hire for the best experience. Gerakas Beach has restricted access after sunset to protect nesting turtles — respect all conservation guidelines. This is your last full day in Greece — savor every moment.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast at your villa or hotel, take a last swim in the Ionian Sea, and pack for departure. Visit a local market or shop for last-minute Greek souvenirs — local honey, olive oil, saffron from Kozani, Mastiha products from Chios, or handmade ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Zakynthos International Airport (Dionysios Solomos Airport) for your return flight to Belgrade via Air Serbia (confirm return flight details). Alternatively, if flying home from Athens, take a short domestic flight from Zakynthos to Athens and connect to your international flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with extraordinary memories of 13 days of beaches, world-class food, ancient history, and Aegean magic.

meals.breakfast: Final luxurious Greek breakfast — fresh bread, local honey, Zakynthian cheese, olives, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a final quick meal at a harbor café in Zakynthos Town before transfer
meals.dinner: Dinner on board your return flight or upon arrival at your home destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. Confirm all return flight details and any luggage restrictions for items purchased (liquids, food products). Ensure all hotel checkouts are completed on time. Consider purchasing travel insurance that covers flight delays and cancellations.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC
